items.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Oscar put us up on the stage together to fight immediately, that very first night he walked into New York.

ctx.x: Do you remember when you first met him?

Yeah, I met him in the [Cafe] Bohemia the first night he came to New York to work with Oscar Pettiford’s band, and Oscar put us up on the stage together to fight immediately, that very first night he walked into New York. I tried to get off the stage, because I was on the stage with Herbie Nichols, playing with him. As I was leaving the stage, Oscar Pettiford said, “No, no, man. Don’t go anywhere. Stay right there. I want you to meet somebody.” And he introduced me to Cannonball. But of course by that time I…
You mentioned playing with Herbie Nichols. I had the impression that Herbie Nichols largely performed outside of the modern jazz context.
